title: `let*` as the last expression of a function is not a tail call when the function allocates locally
summary: `let* a = e in loop (n - 1) a` as the last expression of a function is not compiled as a tail call when the function allocates on the local stack; a comparison of two tuples is enough, with no `local_` in the source. A loop written so ends with `Stack_overflow` in native code; bytecode and OCaml 5.4.0 run it in constant stack.
cause: `Texp_letop` has no position, and `transl_letop` in `lambda/translcore.ml` builds the application of the operator with `Rc_normal` always, so the region of the function is ended after the call returns.

fix.text: Records the position of a let-operator in the typed tree and gives the application of the `let` operator that position. Builds; `test.ml` then prints the expected result; testsuite unchanged.
